title: Trigger the Two Words That Immediately Transform Any Negotiation
coreMove: Summarize the other side so accurately that they feel understood enough to let persuasion begin.
sourcePressure: The source ties this chapter to that's right, summarizing, alignment, and permission to persuade, building on prior recognition and autonomy rather than treating the phrase as magic.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must not make that's right a verbal hack, flattery line, or shortcut around accurate understanding.

hook: Someone says the magic words and the deal unlocks
A clever recap impresses a boss
tryThisNow: Try to get a that's right

exampleSpecs.domain: specialty coffee roaster negotiating green-bean delivery terms
exampleSpecs.audience: a roaster trying to move an importer after weeks of argument about late shipments
exampleSpecs.stakes: a seasonal roast launch may fail if the importer sees only blame
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the roaster summarizes the importer's cash-flow, port-delay, and reputation pressures until the importer says that's right and offers a split-container schedule
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a burlap sample bag cut open beside a roast-profile printout

exampleSpecs.domain: youth soccer league field allocation after rain closures
exampleSpecs.audience: a league director facing coaches who accuse her of favoritism
exampleSpecs.stakes: the season schedule may break if coaches reject the revised field grid
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director summarizes each coach's lost practice nights, parent pressure, and tournament deadline before asking for options, waiting for the first that's right before proposing the grid
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a soaked field-closure sign leaning against a chain-link fence

exampleSpecs.audience: an auctioneer working with heirs who reject a realistic reserve
exampleSpecs.stakes: a valuable collection may fail to sell because grief is hidden under price demands
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the auctioneer summarizes that the reserve is carrying grief, family fairness, and fear of disrespect, and the heirs say that's right before discussing separate lots
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a porcelain appraisal tag tied with cotton string to a cabinet handle

exampleSpecs.domain: regional newspaper subscription dispute with a printing partner
exampleSpecs.audience: a publisher trying to renegotiate print deadlines after missed rural deliveries
exampleSpecs.stakes: cancellations will spike if the partner sees the complaint as one-sided
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a failed demand, the publisher summarizes the printer's labor shortage, press maintenance, and carrier handoff constraints until the printer says that's right and reveals a viable earlier handoff
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stack of unsold papers banded in blue plastic at the depot door

exampleSpecs.domain: aquarium animal-transport permit with state regulators
exampleSpecs.audience: a curator seeking approval for a transfer that regulators keep slowing
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fragile animal may miss the safe transport window if trust does not form
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the curator decides to summarize the regulator's disease-control, public scrutiny, and contingency fears before presenting the revised transport plan
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sealed transport crate checklist clipped above a quarantine tank

exampleSpecs.domain: independent hardware store negotiating a landlord repair contribution
exampleSpecs.audience: a store owner who needs the landlord to share roof-repair costs
exampleSpecs.stakes: inventory will be damaged during the rainy season if both sides stay positional
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the store owner reviews how accurately summarizing the landlord's insurance deductible, tenant precedent, and vacancy fear produced that's right and opened a repair-credit option
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rain-darkened ceiling tile propped beside a stack of inventory invoices

skillTargets: identify what an accurate summary must include before persuasion
distinguish that's right from you're right or polite agreement
analyze whether a proposed summary preserves autonomy
evaluate when the writer is treating the phrase as magic instead of evidence of alignment

tryThisNowSpec: Before making one ask, write a three-part summary of the other side's pressure, constraint, and fear; do not make the ask until the summary could stand on its own.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter
